title: The first waterfall a generated world has ever had
question: Does this read as a waterfall, or as a damp stain on the cliff? I think it is too thin and too dark, and I want to know whether you agree before I spend a round tuning it.
context_md:
Nothing had ever placed a spring in a generated world -- every waterfall shown before now was a test harness putting one there by hand. This is the `springs` worldgen pass placing one on its own.

**It works, by the numbers.** Over three canyon seeds it emits 2.6-4.5M fill units and drains 90-98% of it, so the water genuinely arrives and leaves rather than filling a bath. But looking at it, I am not convinced: the fall hugs the rock face and renders nearly black, because `render.rs` dims a liquid toward black by *fill*, and the drains at the foot take the water almost as fast as it lands so no cell is ever near full.

If you agree it is too thin, the lever I would reach for first is moving the drains further from the plunge pool so a pool actually stands under the fall -- the near drain is 40 columns out, which is basically in the pool.

This is a still, and a fall is a moving thing. Say the word and I will get you a sequence instead.

Canyon, seed 7, world x 7280-7792 at 4x, after 500 frames of settling.

items.label: generated spring, canyon seed 7
items.caption: Outlet at (7388, 99), span 5. The fall is the blue-grey band down the left of the face.
